title: Correct in Isolation: Why Correct Parts Fail Together, and How to Find the Seams

posts.title: A Watch Delayed Becomes a List
The Second Pass Is the Last

specimen.contracts: Kubernetes documented contracts read in October and November 2026; no release is pinned, and where a contract is open the worst case it allows is modelled
specimen.part1: HPA on CPU at the documented tolerance 0.1; VPA recommender margin 0.15, 90th percentile, 24 h half-life
specimen.part2: 16 pods, 8 per node, pod dead time 90 s, node provisioning 210 s, HPA stabilization 300 s, CA unneeded time 600 s
specimen.part3: 2000 informers, 100 seat-seconds per second, 300 s history, watches 300 to 600 s, queue wait limit 15 s
specimen.part4: 9 nodes in 3 zones; webhook 3 replicas, DNS 2, application 3; nodes drained one at a time
specimen.part5: six sets of two or three mutating webhooks on one pod (label, sidecar injector, pull policy, digest pin, signer, capability policy, mesh init, label-selected injector); every order; one to six passes
specimen.part6: the specimens of Parts 1 to 5, one per seam; symmetric loops, start-time cycles and value chains of 3 to 6 members; 150 random dependency graphs of 2 to 4 webhooks
